title: Turn it down

brief.story: The bedside lamp is far too bright at night. It has a 10 kΩ knob (a potentiometer) in series with a fixed 330 Ω, so the brightness can be set without touching the wiring.
brief.goal: Turn RV1’s knob so LED1 runs at a gentle 4.5–5.5 mA.

hints: Select RV1 and turn its knob with ‹ ›. Here the current goes in at leg 1 and out at the wiper, so the knob sets how much of the 10 kΩ track it passes through.
The current is 7 V ÷ (330 Ω + track). For 5 mA the total wants to be 7 V ÷ 0.005 A = 1.4 kΩ.
At 10 % the track is 1 kΩ: 7 V ÷ 1.33 kΩ = 5.3 mA.

spec.explain: Between leg 1 and the wiper, a potentiometer is a resistor whose value the knob sets: 10 kΩ × the position.

debrief: Used from one end to the wiper, a potentiometer is a variable resistor (a rheostat): the knob sets how much of its track is in the loop. The fixed 330 Ω keeps the LED safe when the knob is turned right down to 0 Ω. Dimmers, fan speeds and old volume knobs all started out like this.
